data.text: Scheduler answers 2026-11-11 (operator selections, relayed by coordinator): (1) CLI noun: "Add `jobs` alias". (2) Mutating check actions: "Allow with approval". (3) Condition language: "Richer expression language". (4) Churn excludes lockfiles/generated paths by default: "Yes, configurable". (5) Company jobs audit mode first: "No, enforce immediately".

data.alternatives: Alias rejected-as-rename: renaming 'job' (breaks detached-run users) or a separate 'jobs' noun with its own code (two surfaces). Mutating: read-only forever (the operator declined), auto-approve for unattended runs (rejected: privilege escalation). Language: all/any clauses only (declined); Python eval or a full scripting language (rejected, unsafe, Turing-complete). Churn: count every line (inflated by lockfiles). Company jobs: mandatory audit-first (declined).
data.consequences: (i) ALIAS: 'jobs' must not be confused with 'ddflow job' (detached runs, ddflow_job_*). Help for 'schedule' says: 'recurring and triggered work definitions (alias: jobs); NOT detached runs, see ddflow job'; help for 'job' says: 'detached runs of one command; for recurring definitions see ddflow schedule / jobs'; 'ddflow help' lists both with that one-line contrast; MCP keeps one ddflow_schedule tool, no new noun. Alias is a parser alias only, one code path, a test asserts 'jobs list' equals 'schedule list'. Residual tension: the word job now means two things (a run vs a definition); user-facing text says 'scheduled job' for definitions. (ii) MUTATING ACTIONS: this amends D-trigger-actions-create-items (read-only check) to: read-only by default; a job may declare mutating=true with an explicit command allow-list. Approvals are single-use, bound to command/args/state/directory and expire in 1h, so an unattended run cannot hold a person's approval. Model: (a) creating or editing a mutating job (or flipping mutating on, widening its allow-list, or enabling it) is a guarded config change needing a person's approval at definition time, a job proposed by an agent starts disabled; (b) each mutating RUN files its own approval request and PARKS (item state parked with the request id, recorded schedule.run outcome awaiting_approval, owner and next call per r-alert-owner-next-call), never auto-approves and never blocks the tick; an expired request is unavailable and is refiled at most under the cap; (c) the definition-time approval authorizes the job's shape, never an individual run; (d) the standing approval window and policy auto-approve rules remain the operator's separate, recorded choice and are not implied by this answer; (e) a job cannot create or edit a mutating job, template or its own definition (privilege escalation), job-created items cannot touch schedule definitions without approval; (f) r-bounded-everything caps (timeout, output cap, runs per hour, hop limit, breaker) and r-consent-outward (outward effects need approval each time unless a recorded standing consent exists) still bind; r-untrusted-data: no fact or record text is interpolated into a command. (iii) EXPRESSION LANGUAGE: richer, but it must remain a SAFE, sandboxed, non-Turing-complete evaluator: own parser, no eval/exec/compile, no attribute or item access to Python objects, no imports, no loops or recursion or user-defined functions, typed facts only (int, float, bool, str, duration, timestamp, list, UNAVAILABLE), a pure-function allow-list (min, max, abs, len, contains, startswith, endswith, any, all over bounded lists, days_since, ratio), bounded source length (default 512 chars), AST depth (16), node count (128), list size, string size, and a node-count evaluation budget with a visible stop (r-bounded-everything). Errors are definition-time refusals, a runtime budget hit is UNAVAILABLE, and UNAVAILABLE propagates (a condition with an unavailable fact is unavailable, never true or false by accident). Shape: a CEL-like subset (facts.churn_lines >= 500 && !facts.ci_red). The declarative all/any form stays valid as sugar that compiles to the same AST. Reuse: check services/guidance and services/approvals/policy.py predicate and fact facilities first and reuse their fact registry and operator semantics if they exist; extend, do not build a second matcher. Libraries: candidates are cel-python (celpy), simpleeval, asteval, jsonlogic; zero-dependency option is a hand-written Pratt parser over a closed grammar (~300 lines), recommended default because it gives exact control of limits and keeps r-adapters dependency rules (stdlib-only core; third-party code only behind an adapter, declared and pinned). simpleeval and asteval are rejected as defaults (they wrap Python's ast, a larger attack surface); celpy is acceptable only as an optional adapter. Nothing is installed by this decision. Fuzz and hostile-input tests are required. (iv) CHURN EXCLUDES: lines-changed counts skip by default lockfiles (uv.lock, poetry.lock, package-lock.json, yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml, Cargo.lock, go.sum), generated golden snapshots, pins files, vendored and generated paths (vendor/, third_party/, node_modules/, dist/, build/, *.min.js, *_pb2.py, *.generated.*, snapshots). Configurable per job (churn_exclude, churn_include) and per layer ([schedule_jobs].churn_exclude); literal globs only; layers add or replace by D-config-layer-order; schedule show prints the effective exclude list and the count of lines excluded so the number is explainable. (v) COMPANY JOBS: enforce from the first release. D-GP-Q5 (new company policy audits one release first) is SUPERSEDED FOR SCHEDULED JOBS ONLY and stays in force for graded policies and rules; recorded as a scoped amendment, not a repeal. A company-policy job acts from its first release; the user is still highest (D-user-highest-precedence-2026-11-06): a person may override a company job locally with an explicit, recorded override (who, why, scope, optional expiry), shown in status and brief; agents and project files can never override it; locked=true requires the explicit person-only act, locked=false may be overridden in the user or local layer. Company jobs that are mutating are still subject to (ii): a company job cannot pre-approve a run, each mutating run still files its own approval. Because enforcement is immediate, schedule show and a dry-run verb ('schedule run --dry-run') must exist for a company author before publishing; audit mode stays available as an optional per-job flag audit=true that a company author may choose, not a mandatory first release.
data.context: 13 SJ-* tasks and B-schedule-cli-not-registered came out of the scheduler research. These five questions were open. Standing decisions: D-sched-no-daemon-r2, D-sched-triggers-separate, D-trigger-actions-create-items (a job files items or runs a read-only check), D-config-layer-order, D-user-highest-precedence-2026-11-06, D-GP-Q5.
data.decision: Operator 2026-11-11 on R-scheduler-2026-11-11: (1) 'ddflow jobs' is an alias of 'ddflow schedule'. (2) A job action may run mutating commands, each under a recorded approval. (3) The job condition is a richer expression language, not only declarative all/any clauses. (4) Churn thresholds exclude lockfiles and generated paths by default, configurable. (5) Company-policy jobs enforce from their first release (no audit-first); a person can still override locally.
data.title: Scheduler answers: jobs alias, mutating actions with approval, expression language, churn excludes, company jobs enforce at once

data.consequences: SJ-company-jobs drops mandatory audit mode; authors need a dry-run before publishing. See D-scheduler-answers-2026-11-11.
data.decision: Operator 2026-11-11: company-policy scheduled jobs enforce from their first release. D-GP-Q5 (audit one release first) stays for graded policies and rules and is superseded for scheduled jobs only. Audit remains an optional per-job flag. The user override of D-user-highest-precedence-2026-11-06 still applies.
data.title: D-GP-Q5 audit-first does not apply to company-policy scheduled jobs

data.consequences: SJ-actions, SJ-job-security, SJ-tick amended; anti-escalation tests required. See D-scheduler-answers-2026-11-11 (ii).
data.decision: Operator 2026-11-11: a job action is read-only by default and may declare mutating=true with a command allow-list; each mutating run files its own approval and parks until a person answers; creating, editing or enabling a mutating job needs a person's approval; no auto-approve. Widens the read-only check of D-trigger-actions-create-items; item-filing triggers are unchanged.
data.title: Scheduled job actions may run mutating commands, each under a recorded approval

data.body: SIZE M, RISK high (sandbox). Split from SJ-when by the operator's answer 3 (richer expression language). A hand-written Pratt parser over a CLOSED grammar producing a typed AST: literals (int, float, bool, str, duration, timestamp, list), fact references (facts.NAME), comparison, and/or/not (&& || !), in, arithmetic + - * /, ternary-free, and a pure-function allow-list (min, max, abs, len, contains, startswith, endswith, any, all over bounded lists, days_since, ratio). NOT Turing-complete: no loops, recursion, assignment, user functions, imports, attribute or item access to Python objects, no eval/exec/compile, no ast.literal_eval shortcuts. Limits with visible stops: source length 512, AST depth 16, node count 128, list size 32, string size 256. The declarative all/any form is accepted and compiles to the same AST. Definition-time refusals name the position and reason; unknown fact or function refused. Check services/guidance and services/approvals/policy.py for a shared predicate or fact facility first and say what was reused; no second matcher. Dependency rule (r-adapters): zero-dependency default; a library (celpy, simpleeval, asteval) only behind an adapter, not installed here. Acceptance: grammar table tests, depth/size/length limits, hostile and fuzz inputs (dunder access, __import__, huge nesting, unicode confusables, very long literals, deep lists, recursion bombs; a seeded property fuzz asserting no exception other than the typed refusal, bounded time), declarative form equals expression form. Part of R-scheduler-2026-11-11 and D-scheduler-answers-2026-11-11. Hard limits: no daemon (D-sched-no-daemon-r2); verbs ride B-sched-author's family, do not edit cli.py, mcp.py or config.py; literal globs only. Every cap is bounded with a visible stop (r-bounded-everything). Tests fail before the change, fake clock.
data.title: Job condition language: closed grammar, parser, definition-time validation, safety limits, fuzz tests

data.body:
SIZE M, RISK med. The validation rule of a job: when = {all|any: [{fact, op(<,<=,==,>=,>,in), value}]}, plus not. Pure function over SJ-facts, no expression language, no eval, no shell (OPA/Cedar-style data, not code). UNAVAILABLE fact makes the whole condition unavailable and the job reports it rather than firing or passing silently. Every evaluation, including false, is a logged event with the fact values (audit, like trigger.evaluated). Reuse services/approvals/policy.py predicate conventions rather than a second matcher; check guidance engine for a shared matcher first and say what was reused. Acceptance: truth table, nested all/any, unavailable propagation, malformed predicate refused at definition time. Part of R-scheduler-2026-11-11. Hard limits: no daemon (D-sched-no-daemon-r2); a job only files items or runs a read-only check (D-trigger-actions-create-items); verbs ride B-sched-author's family, do not edit cli.py, mcp.py or config.py; literal globs only. Every cap is bounded with a visible stop (r-bounded-everything). Tests fail before the change, fake clock.

AMENDED by D-scheduler-answers-2026-11-11 (answer 3): SIZE now M, RISK high. The condition is the richer sandboxed expression language, NOT only all/any clauses; the grammar, parser and definition-time validation moved to SJ-when-grammar, this task is the evaluator. Evaluate the AST over SJ-facts with typed facts only, a per-evaluation node budget with a visible stop (a budget hit is UNAVAILABLE, never true), UNAVAILABLE propagates through and/or/not/functions per a documented truth table. Every evaluation, including false, is logged with the fact values. Extra acceptance: hostile expressions from the grammar fuzz corpus evaluate to a typed refusal or UNAVAILABLE within the time bound; evaluation never calls anything but the allow-listed pure functions.
data.title: Job condition evaluator: typed facts, UNAVAILABLE propagation, bounded evaluation budget, evaluation audit events (language from SJ-when-grammar)

data.body:
SIZE M, RISK high. B-sched-run files items; this adds the other action kinds without a new execution path: check = a command from the allow-listed [schedule_jobs].check_commands run through cmdrunner with a timeout and output cap, outcome ok|findings|failed|unavailable recorded as schedule.run evidence (never an agent, never writes the tree); bug = ddflow bug found with dedupe key; notify = through the notify port with owner, next call and dedupe key (r-alert-owner-next-call); note = session note. Spawning an agent run stays with the lane launcher and D-dispatch-modes: the action files a kind=job item and the executor (P-schedule.unattended) may dispatch it. Open question for the operator: may a check run mutating commands? Default no. Acceptance: each kind has a failing-first test; a check that times out is unavailable; command not on the allow-list refused. Part of R-scheduler-2026-11-11. Hard limits: no daemon (D-sched-no-daemon-r2); a job only files items or runs a read-only check (D-trigger-actions-create-items); verbs ride B-sched-author's family, do not edit cli.py, mcp.py or config.py; literal globs only. Every cap is bounded with a visible stop (r-bounded-everything). Tests fail before the change, fake clock.

AMENDED by D-scheduler-answers-2026-11-11 (answer 2), SIZE now L, RISK high: supersedes the 'default no' open question. A job action is read-only by default; mutating=true is declared per job with a command allow-list ([schedule_jobs].mutating_commands, empty by default). Creating, editing, widening or enabling a mutating job needs a person's approval at definition time (guarded config change) and an agent-proposed job starts disabled. Each mutating RUN files its own approval request (single-use, bound to command/args/state/directory, expires in 1h) and PARKS: the item is parked with the request id, schedule.run outcome awaiting_approval, owner and next call recorded (r-alert-owner-next-call); never auto-approved, never blocks the tick; an expired request is unavailable and refiled at most under the cap. The standing approval window / policy auto-approve rules stay the operator's separate choice. Run mutating commands only through cmdrunner with timeout and output cap, no shell interpolation of fact or record text (r-untrusted-data), outward effects still r-consent-outward. Acceptance additions: mutating command without approval never runs; run with approval runs once and the approval is consumed; expired approval = unavailable; a mutating command not on the allow-list refused; read-only check that tries a write is refused or reported. Amends D-trigger-actions-create-items via D-trigger-actions-mutating-approved-2026-11-11.

SIZE M, RISK high. Jobs are a privilege-escalation path. Threat model and enforced checks: (1) an agent-proposed job, trigger or watch starts disabled and only a person enables it (D-sched-triggers-separate); (2) editing a job definition is a guarded config change (services/approvals/config_guard.py); (3) a job acts with its recorded class, never the creator's or a session's authority; actions touching dependencies, security, architecture, outward effects need approval each time unless a recorded standing consent exists (r-consent-outward, standing approval window); (4) check commands only from the allow-list, no shell interpolation of fact or record text (r-untrusted-data); (5) a company locked job cannot be weakened by project files; (6) hop limit and breaker still bind job-created items. Acceptance: one failing-first test per attack (agent sets enabled, template sets layer, record text injected into a command, job files a task that edits its own definition, job loop via its own failure). Independent cross-family review required. Part of R-scheduler-2026-11-11. Hard limits: no daemon (D-sched-no-daemon-r2); a job only files items or runs a read-only check (D-trigger-actions-create-items); verbs ride B-sched-author's family, do not edit cli.py, mcp.py or config.py; literal globs only. Every cap is bounded with a visible stop (r-bounded-everything). Tests fail before the change, fake clock.

AMENDED by D-scheduler-answers-2026-11-11 (answer 2), SIZE now L: mutating-with-approval is the main new attack surface. Added checks, each with a failing-first regression test: (7) an agent cannot create, edit, widen, or enable a mutating job; flipping mutating=true is a guarded change a person approves; (8) a job, template, company job or project file cannot pre-approve its own runs and approvals are never auto-granted for scheduled runs; (9) a mutating run with an expired, reused or mismatched approval (other args, directory or state) does not run; (10) a job-created item cannot edit schedule definitions without approval (already case 4, extended to mutating); (11) expression language escape attempts (see SJ-when-grammar fuzz corpus) cannot reach Python objects or run a command; (12) caps and breaker bind mutating runs; (13) company jobs: a project file cannot weaken a locked company job, a person-only override is recorded; (14) the 'jobs' alias gives no extra authority. Needs add SJ-when-grammar.

SIZE M, RISK med. Found by R-scheduler-2026-11-11: triggers.evaluate is reachable only from api.schedule.trigger_evaluate and nothing calls it automatically. This task is the single entry point: tick(now) evaluates due schedules (B-sched-due) and event triggers (B-trigger-model), files items, writes trigger.evaluated, under a lock with a time budget and the global hourly cap; callers: brief, session start, after worktree.merged and item completion, loop ticks, and the CLI/MCP verb 'schedule tick' for external schedulers (B-sched-emitters prints the line that runs it; ADP-scheduler registers it). No daemon. Concurrent ticks collapse to one (lease on the tick). Acceptance: two ticks at once file once; a tick after 10 days of outage files once per job (missed policy), no storm; a tick on a clean repo costs no git call beyond the facts requested. Part of R-scheduler-2026-11-11. Hard limits: no daemon (D-sched-no-daemon-r2); a job only files items or runs a read-only check (D-trigger-actions-create-items); verbs ride B-sched-author's family, do not edit cli.py, mcp.py or config.py; literal globs only. Every cap is bounded with a visible stop (r-bounded-everything). Tests fail before the change, fake clock.

AMENDED by D-scheduler-answers-2026-11-11 (answer 2): when a due job is mutating, the tick files the approval request and parks the run instead of running it, records schedule.run outcome awaiting_approval, and the next tick does not refile while the request is pending or after it was answered (idempotent per job+sha+approval); the tick never waits on a person and never auto-approves; parked runs are listed in brief with owner and next call. Acceptance additions: tick with a mutating due job files exactly one request across repeated ticks; approved request later runs once; a rejected or expired request is recorded and obeys the cap and the breaker; tick time budget is unaffected by parked runs.
